skill.name: signup-flow-cro
skill.description: Helps improve signup, registration, account creation, and trial activation flows by reducing friction and clarifying next steps.
skill.summary: Optimize signup flow completion with focused CRO guidance for fields, copy, trust signals, and experiments.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The two static findings are false positives from benign signup optimization guidance in SKILL.md. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, unsafe tool use, or business logic abuse was found.

static_findings.snippet: - Show strength meter instead of rigid rules

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 17 lists paid account creation as a signup flow type. It does not request host inspection, credentials, network access, or system reconnaissance.
Line 81 recommends a password strength meter as user experience guidance. It does not instruct the agent to inspect passwords, systems, files, or secrets.

content.value_statement: Signup friction lowers account creation and trial activation rates. This skill gives focused CRO guidance for fields, copy, trust signals, mobile UX, and experiments.
actual_capabilities: Audits signup forms for friction, unclear copy, weak trust signals, and mobile usability issues.
Recommends field reduction, progressive profiling, social auth, and password UX improvements.
Maps single-step and multi-step signup patterns to B2B, B2C, waitlist, and commerce flows.
Suggests A/B test ideas for form layout, messaging, verification, and trial commitment.
Defines metrics for completion rate, field drop-off, error rate, and time to complete.
limitations: It does not run analytics queries or inspect production event data by itself.
It cannot guarantee conversion lift without controlled tests and sufficient traffic.
It gives UX recommendations, not legal advice for privacy, consent, or compliance requirements.
It needs context about audience, required data, and current drop-off points for best results.

use_cases.title: Improve SaaS Trial Signup
use_cases.description: Identify fields, copy, and trust elements that may reduce free trial starts.

use_cases.title: Reduce Mobile Registration Drop-Off
use_cases.description: Review mobile form layout, keyboard behavior, autofill support, and validation patterns.

use_cases.title: Plan Signup Experiments
use_cases.description: Turn signup issues into prioritized quick wins and A/B test hypotheses.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Signup Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner audit of a signup flow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this signup flow and list the main friction points. Focus on required fields, copy, trust signals, and mobile usability.

prompt_templates.title: Field Reduction Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of required signup data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze these signup fields and decide which are essential, optional, or better collected after account creation.

prompt_templates.title: Multi-Step Flow Redesign
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced redesign for a longer registration flow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Redesign this multi-step signup flow. Recommend step order, field grouping, progress cues, error handling, and post-submit next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Experiment Roadmap
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced CRO planning with measurement needs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a signup optimization roadmap using these analytics. Prioritize quick wins, high-impact changes, and A/B tests with success metrics.

output_examples.input: A B2B trial signup asks for email, password, name, company, phone, team size, and role.
output: High priority: defer phone and team size until onboarding unless sales contact is required.
Medium priority: test Google or Microsoft sign-up as the primary option.
Measurement: track field-level errors and drop-off before and after the change.

output_examples.input: A mobile registration flow has three screens and requires email verification before product access.
output: High priority: allow limited product access before verification when risk allows it.
Medium priority: add a progress indicator and clear resend option.
Test idea: compare immediate verification against delayed verification for activation rate.

output_examples.input: A waitlist page asks for email, company, budget, timeline, and a long use case description.
output: High priority: ask for email first and make the other questions optional.
Medium priority: replace the long text field with one short use case question.
Copy improvement: explain what happens after joining the waitlist.

best_practices: Start with the smallest required field set and collect extra details later.
Track field-level drop-off, errors, and completion time before changing the flow.
Match recommendations to flow type, audience intent, compliance needs, and activation goals.
anti_patterns: Do not require business details that are not needed before first product value.
Do not hide password rules until after the user submits the form.
Do not treat signup completion as success without measuring activation after signup.

faq.question: What signup flows does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports free trials, freemium accounts, paid accounts, waitlists, B2B registration, and B2C registration.

faq.question: Can it improve a checkout account flow?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review whether account creation should happen before, during, or after checkout.

faq.question: Does it replace analytics tools?
faq.answer: No. It uses your analytics context and recommends what metrics to review or track.

faq.question: Can it write signup form copy?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest labels, helper text, button text, error messages, and confirmation copy.

faq.question: Does it handle post-signup onboarding?
faq.answer: It covers immediate post-submit steps, but deeper onboarding optimization needs a separate onboarding review.

faq.question: Can it support A/B testing plans?
faq.answer: Yes. It can turn signup issues into test hypotheses, priorities, and success metrics.
